title: Cyrus and the Witness
premise: Felix Montrose, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made her both brilliant and isolated, receives two letters about the thirty-year-old Harrowgate fire: one confessing to arson, the other promising a fortune for silence. As she investigates, she discovers the confessor is her estranged mentor Cyrus Bell, and the second letter comes from someone who knows Felix witnessed the fire as a child—a memory she has buried. Torn between loyalty to the man who taught her everything and the truth that could free an innocent man convicted of the crime, Felix reconstructs the alibis woven three decades ago and finds they were built to protect someone she loves. In the end, she testifies to what she truly saw, clearing the convicted man at the cost of Cyrus's freedom—and finally claims a place among people who know her whole story.
about_author: S. M. Ravensworth is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent fifteen years reading other people's disasters before writing her own. She lives in a coastal town where fog is frequent and secrets are longer-lived.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: POV Felix. On an ordinary Tuesday, Felix receives twin letters about the Harrowgate fire—both written in handwriting she recognizes instantly as Cyrus Bell's, though one confesses and one promises payment for silence. Her photographic memory flags the discrepancy in ink age. The emotional beat is unease: the past has found her address.

chapters.title: The Man Who Taught Me to See
chapters.summary: POV Felix, with flashback. Felix traces her career back to Cyrus, the investigator who trained her eye and then vanished from her life twelve years ago. She visits his shuttered office and finds case files on the Harrowgate fire—files he was never assigned. The beat is longing tangled with suspicion; love and doubt share the same room.

chapters.title: What the Child Saw
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Digging into sealed juvenile records, Felix confronts a suppressed memory: she lived near Harrowgate as a girl and may have seen the fire's true origin. Fragments surface unbidden—her memory never forgets, only hides. The beat is dread as she realizes she isn't investigating the case; she is the case.

chapters.title: The Convicted Man's Daughter
chapters.summary: POV alternating Felix and Nell Okafor, daughter of the man imprisoned for the fire. Nell hires Felix unofficially, believing the confession letter proves her father innocent. Their wary alliance forms over shared coffee and mutual distrust. The beat is tentative belonging—two strangers bound by the same old fire.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Twice
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Reconstructing the night of the fire, Felix finds every witness statement aligns too perfectly—three alibis sharing identical phrasing, as if rehearsed. Someone coached them all, and the coaching matches Cyrus's methods. The beat is betrayal sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Second Letter's Sender
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Following paper trails and a postmark, Felix identifies the sender of the promise-of-silence letter: Margaret Harrowgate herself, the widow whose insurance claim Felix's firm once denied. Margaret offers Felix money and a warning—the truth will cost her Cyrus. The beat is temptation made flesh.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Breakwater
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix corners Cyrus on the breakwater where he once taught her to read tides. He admits writing the confession but refuses to explain, insisting some truths protect more people than they hurt. The beat is heartbreak: loyalty pulling against truth with equal force, and Felix unable to let either win.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: POV Nell, with Felix present. Nell uncovers her father's hidden ledger showing payments received before the fire—he was paid to be elsewhere, not to burn anything. The payer's initials match Margaret's late husband. The beat is vertigo: the conspiracy protected the Harrowgates, and Cyrus took the fall's weight onto himself.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Felix. At the pre-trial hearing, Felix takes the stand and unlocks her buried memory under oath: she saw Margaret's husband leave the boathouse minutes before the flames. The courtroom holds its breath as her perfect recall becomes both weapon and wound. The beat is the climax—truth spoken at last, whatever it destroys.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: POV Felix, epilogue months later. Cyrus accepts a reduced sentence for obstruction; Nell's father walks free, and Nell and Felix share a quiet meal that feels like family. Felix closes her notebook on the case she couldn't keep invisible and opens a new page. The beat is resolution: belonging earned through truth, not silence.
